chunks: He is Allah, the True, the Manifester of Truth.
He is more True and more manifest than eyes can see.
Intellects cannot comprehend Him by fixing limits for Him since in that case to Him would be attribute shape.
Imagination cannot catch Him by fixing quantities for Him for in that case to Him would be attributed body.
He created creatures without any example, and without the advice of a counsel, or the assistance of a helper.
His creation was completed by His command, and bowed to His obedience.
It responded (to Him) and did not defy (Him). It obeyed and did not resist.
ai.seo_question: How does Nahj al-Balagha describe Allah's transcendence beyond human perception and physical form?
ai.summary: This passage from Imam Ali’s sermon in Nahj al-Balagha articulates the Shia doctrine of *Tawhid* by distinguishing between Allah’s essential reality (*Dhat*) and His attributes, asserting that He is 'Al-Haqq al-Mubin' (The Manifest Truth) beyond the reach of sensory perception or intellectual definition. It emphasizes *La Tashbih wa La Takyif* (no resemblance and no modality), clarifying that creation occurred through His sovereign command (*Amr*) without consultation (*Mashura*) or assistance (*Ma'una*), a concept central to Shia theological discourse on divine autonomy. The text serves as a profound meditation on the contrast between the finite, obedient creation and the infinite, self-sufficient Creator.
